# ‘Only fools are not afraid’: Ukrainians adapt to life under constant Russian drone attacks

![People clear debris at a market hit by a Russian drone strike on April 4, 2026, in Nikopol, Ukraine.](https://media.cnn.com/api/v1/images/stellar/prod/gettyimages-2269888116.jpg?c=16x9&q=w_1383,c_fill)

Nikopol, in southern [Ukraine](https://www.cnn.com/world/europe/ukraine), rarely makes the headlines – overshadowed by the threats to the occupied Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant directly across the river. But this city on the front line of Russia’s full-scale invasion has been attacked almost every day since the war began, local authorities say.

Its proximity to Russian military positions only two miles away on the other bank of the Dnipro River means that [civilians face a heightened risk](https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/europe/ukraine-civilian-deaths-russia-war-intl) of attacks by short-range Russian drones.

“We’ve actually grown somewhat accustomed to the danger, though the feeling of fear never really goes away,” said Oleksandr Varytsev, a poet who also runs a local charity that provides hot meals for elderly and disabled people. “It’s very scary – and if it’s scary for me, you can imagine how older men and women feel when they come to our volunteer center.”

Horrifying video posted by authorities in June showed a small Russian drone target an elderly woman in a wheelchair – an attack that killed three people, including the 87-year-old woman and

events.content_detail:
# US Universities Got Over $300M From Sanctioned China Entities

Published

Jul 18, 2026 at 04:00 AM EDT

![Didi Kirsten Tatlow](/default-avatar.svg)

Senior Correspondent, International Affairs

Spooked by a decades-long outflow of top Amerian science and technology to adversaries, the Department of Education has disclosed new data on donations to American [universities](/topic/universities) by foreign companies and universities that today are sanctioned by the U.S., including 527 donations from Chinese entities.

A spreadsheet of 697 donations in total, obtained by *Newsweek*, is titled "Counterparties of Concern" and includes 156 donations to U.S. universities from Chinese technology giant Huawei and its U.S. subsidary FutureWei, totaling $42 million. Also prominent among donors was the Beijing Institute of Technology (BIT), one China's "Seven Sons of National Defense" military-affiliated universities, which donated more than $49 million.

The data aims to increase transparency in the U.S. and help end influence, as well as technology and knowledge outflow to China, said research security expert Jeffrey Stoff, President of the Center for Research Security & Integrity. Universities were not disclosing all donations, Stoff told *Newsweek*. "They [Department of Education] intend to enforce the reporting rules more aggressively," he said.

# 3 Emerging Market Mining Stocks Investors Are Watching As Tariffs Reroute Global Trade

Global tariffs have scrambled trade routes and pricing power, and many U.S. focused exporters are now facing higher costs and weaker demand. At the same time, a different group is coming into focus: emerging market exporters that sit outside the tariff crossfire and may pick up business as trade is diverted away from the U.S. This article looks at three stocks from that Non U.S. Emerging Market Exporters screener that appear closely tied to the current trade shake up, and explains why some investors might see them as potential beneficiaries to watch or avoid.

## Antam (Persero) (IDX:ANTM)

**Overview:** Antam (Persero) is a Jakarta based, state linked metals and mining company that explores, mines, refines, and markets nickel, gold, silver, bauxite, alumina, and other minerals for both domestic and export customers, with activities that stretch from raw ore to processed metals and related services.

**Operations:** Antam (Persero) generates most of its revenue from Precious Metals and Refinery at IDR 69,129,231 million, followed by Nickel at IDR 15,552,912 million and Bauxite and Alumina at IDR 3,085,957 million, with sales primarily in Indonesia at IDR 84,588,635 million and exports of IDR 3,225,441 million.

**Market Cap:** IDR 73,794.5 billion
